To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the hepatocyte-specific cell surface component gp105 is expressed on the bile canalicular membranes of normal hepatocytes, and is not expressed on two transplantable rat liver carcinoma cells.
a family of glycopeptides (gp105) is expressed by normal hepatocytes but is not expressed by 253 and 310 hepatoma cells.
the expression of gp105 is altered in two transplantable rat liver carcinomas.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the characterization of a novel family of cell surface glycoproteins, gp105, that is associated with the bile canaliculus of normal rat hepatocytes and is not expressed by two hepatocellular carcinoma cell lines.
the characterization of the expression of cell-surface proteins in normal rat liver and two transplantable hepatocellular carcinogenesis (253 and 1111c).
the identification and characterization of cell surface glycoproteins on rat liver cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of gp105 by hepatocytes and its loss of expression by hepatocellular carcinoma cell lines is a useful marker for the differentiation of hepatocytes and hepatocellular carcinoma.

these results indicate that the loss or altered expression of a normal hepatocyte cell-surface glycoprotein is associated with a loss of normal hepatocyte function in two transplantable hepatocellular carcinoma cell lines.
the expression of gp105 by the hepatocytes of the liver is a normal phenomenon that is lost in the hepatocellular carcinoma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have characterized a new family of glycoprotein components that are expressed on the surface of normal hepatocytes and are not expressed on 2 transplantable rat hepatoma cell lines.
the altered expression or loss of expression of a normal cell-surface component may be associated with malignant transformation of rat hepatocytes.
the altered expression and/or localization of cell-surface components is associated with abnormal cell growth in the 253 and 310c transplantable rat hepatomas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have developed a new model for studying the molecular basis of hepatocellular carcinogenesis.
there is a family of proteins on the surface of normal hepatocytes that are not expressed by two different hepatocellular carcinoma cell lines.
there are differences in the cell surface glycoproteins of normal hepatocytes and hepatocellular carcinomatous cells.
